note: Lesson is the بخرَب / بخرِّب (get-ruined vs ruin) verb pair; from ~35:00 on Medi's Arabic is Latin-transliterated by the engine and many of his lines are '[speaking Arabic]' holes (18:14-22:42, 30:30-36:36), so several kept rows rest on Amal's reaction alone and carry confidence low. D8 and D19 are the same slip (بتفتحي at 26:12) found at two timestamps; kept once as D8. D17 and D18 are the same misunderstanding (pointer ending added to a verb whose noun is the subject) three minutes apart; both kept, both filed C2. No rows added: the agreed rows are invisible to me and every further candidate I saw (12:24 تحت الكلمة, 16:03 خربات, 18:04 صححته, 37:35 ثانورك, 38:53 غرفةك, 42:33 مش كان, 44:39 echarrab) is likely already agreed.

rulings.why: S5 restart, not a form error: at 05:33 he is asking ('روس شمال؟ Did you say? رو... شس...') while retrieving the word he had already said right at 05:02 and 05:10 (شمال روسيا); Amal's 05:37 fix targets the el- on شمال (the agreed A2 slip), not the country name. The one time he used روس inside a finished sentence (06:02) is ruled in D15.

row.medi_said: برد كتير ويكون بيمطر أو بتثلج.
row.why: Two slips in one phrase, so both readers are right: يكون without b- in a plain statement right after he had said بيكون at 06:02 (B1), and masculine بيمطر where her sheet has 'it's raining | Betma66er | بتمطر' while he got بتثلج right (B18); she only echoed مطر، ثلج and let it pass.
row.english: it's very cold and it rains or snows

row.why: English calque 'kind of cloudy': نوع is 'type / kind | Noa3 | نوع' on her sheet and does not mean 'somewhat'; her word for a bit is 'a little / a bit | Shwai | شوي'; she let it pass and at 07:10-07:18 modelled الدنيا ... مغيمة وعتمة without نوع. Separate from the agreed مغني-for-مغيم slip in the same line.

row.medi_said: is it أنجم؟ I don't know. أنجم، نجوم،
row.why: She asked 'What's multiple?' of نجمة (sheet 'star | Nejme | نجمة'); he first repeated نجمة, then invented the pattern أنجم and offered نجوم as an alternative, and she confirmed نجوم. READER-BRIEF files 'wrong plural pattern he invented' under vocab tier 2, so vocab-A tier 2 rather than grammar A9.

row.amal_said: قبل ما نزيد بيه، شو بنقيم؟
row.why: She said بنقيم (we remove the -aan) at 11:10 and he echoed it as بنعيد (we repeat) three times (11:11, 11:25, 11:47); she re-said بنقيم at 12:02 while spelling out the steps; sheet 'i remove / take away | Ba2eem | بقيم'. A mis-echo of her meta-verb; the engine may have shaped his word, so low and kept apart as listening.

row.medi_said: with AC, can I say that? Air conditioning. تباي.
row.amal_said: مم. تبعيت. We don't-- We haven't discussed تبعيت a lot yet. So تبعيت.
row.right: تبعي (her form transcribed as تبعيت, possibly تبعتي)
row.why: He tried the possessive particle تبع + my-ending for 'my AC' and asked 'can I say that?'; she recast the form three times (transcribed تبعيت, likely تبعتي or تبعي) and said they had not covered it much. Possession-marker construction = A4, not a lexical item; low because her form is garbled and his تباي may be only تبعي with the ع softened (which would be S4).

row.amal_said: So it's, it's, it's just إشي. Everything my girlfriend, my fiancée uses. So it's one thing.
row.why: Asked to repeat 'anything she uses stops working' (20:40, 20:44) he put a plural after كل; she stressed 'just إشي ... one thing' and at 21:53 modelled كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب. Real fix, but his own line is a transcript hole, so low.

Repeating the rice sentence one minute after her fix ما بتحطي (25:08) he again used فتح (open) for حط (put): sheet 'put | 7ott | حط' vs 'he opened | huwwe fata7 | هو فتح'; she answered ممتاز (26:25). Same slip as D19, which is dropped as a duplicate; the word sits in the 26:12 line, not the 26:04 one.
row.english: if you don't put it (in the fridge)

rulings.why: Cannot be verified - transcript hole: at 25:08-25:18 he built the same slot as بي / الـ / ثلاجة (= بالثلاجة, preposition present), and the 26:17 هي is most plausibly the engine's hearing of في/بـ before الثلاجة; Amal said ممتاز. The missing object -ه is not chargeable either: her own model at 25:08 was ما بتحطي... without it.

row.why: Didn't-know: he asked (شو يعني تذاكر) what the plural in her example سفرتنا خربت لأنه ما في تذاكر meant and she glossed 'tickets'; sheet 'ticket | Tazkara | تذكرة'. READER-BRIEF reserves mode=listening for drills where he misread her Arabic aloud; a meaning question is an asked/tier-0 row in the default speaking mode.

row.medi_said: So don't break it. I mean, you could use that as a command, right? ... Well, don't make it stop working, right? Not don't stop working.
row.amal_said: Don't break something would be the other one. ... مم، no, it would be don't stop working.
row.wrong: ما تخرب = don't break it / don't make it stop working
row.right: ما تخرب = don't stop working (don't get ruined); ما تخرّب = don't break it
row.why: For the second time in the lesson (first at 13:10) he read the plain form as the causative; she said no twice (32:08, 32:28) and named the doubled verb as 'the other one' for don't break something. It is the make-X vs get-X distinction the lesson drills, voiced by her as an explicit no.
row.english: don't break it (vs don't stop working)

row.medi_said: Uh, shu, shu ahki? Shu tehki? Shu haket li? ... haket li. Shu haket li?
row.why: Asking Amal (f) 'what did you say to me' needs the you-f past ending -ti: sheet 'you (f) talked | inti 7akaiti | إنتي حكيتي'; he said haket (the I / you-m form) three times in a row, and she answered the content ('I said صح') without fixing the form.
row.english: what did you say to me?

row.medi_said: uh, bidullu, bidullu, um, yikharabu. Keeps, uh, yikharabu?
row.amal_said: Mm-mm, no. [speaks Arabic] ... So they are what's breaking. Did you break them?
row.why: For 'why do your keys keep breaking' he said bidullu yikharabu; she said no, her fix is a transcript hole, and his follow-up 'they stop working, not they... or someone breaking it?' plus her 'so they are what's breaking' show the no was about the get-X / make-X shape of the verb. Low because her corrected form is not transcribed.

row.medi_said: آآآ، اليوم أكلت آآآ، رز مع دجاج teriyaki،
row.why: MSA form دجاج for a word he knows in her dialect form: sheet 'chicken | Jaj | جاج' and 'chicken | Jaaje | جاجة'; she answered صحتين and let it pass. Low because the engine may have MSA-normalised what he said; for Amal's review page.

Twenty seconds after her second fix (05:37 بس شمال روسيا, which he repeated right at 05:41) he opened his own sentence with el- on the first word of the idafa again, and clipped روسيا to روس; she let this third instance pass.

rulings.why: Cannot be verified: narrating the derivation ('end of the word, then ... add a b-') his 12:37 مزيد is most plausibly منزيد / بنزيد ('we add') with the m-/bn- prefix collapsed by the engine, and the m- 'we' prefix is itself a Levantine variant, not a wrong word; Amal answered مم and moved on. Not an error I can prove from the transcript.

row.medi_said: Uh, do I need to do it for this verb too? ... Yeah, [speaking Arabic]
row.amal_said: بس. بيخرب. بس بيخرب. ... No, because it breaks. يعني خلاص it's kind of another sentence within the sentence. So كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب.
row.why: After she added the pointer -ه to بتستعمله (21:26) he asked whether the second verb needs it too and said the sentence with the ending on بيخرب; she cut in 'بس بيخرب ... No, because it breaks' - كل إشي is the subject of بيخرب, so no pointer. Real explicit no; low because his line is a transcript hole.

row.medi_said: Is it يخربوا؟ Do I need to link it back to the روز؟
row.amal_said: بيخرب. Yes. If you don't-- wait. No. Because the rose is in the beginning. So rose راح يخرب.
row.why: He had said الروز راح يخرب right at 25:36, then doubted it and proposed a pointer ending ('link it back to the روز' - the engine wrote يخربوا); she said no, the rice is the subject at the front, so راح يخرب. Same misreading of the pointer rule as D17, so C2 rather than B18; low because it was offered as a question, not asserted.

rulings.why: Duplicate of D8: the same بتفتحي-for-بتحطي slip in the same sentence; the wrong word sits in the 26:12 line (r1's t), the 26:04 line is only 'Okay. روز راح يخرب إذا،'.

Not provable as his slip: he said الروز with el- at 24:38 and 25:36, and the bare روز at 26:04 is a direct echo of Amal's own 'So rose راح يخرب' seven seconds earlier (25:57); a dropped الـ in the engine's hearing is as likely as a real drop, and she said ممتاز.

Not an error: الغرف is the valid plural 'the rooms' and 'I messed up the rooms by accident' is a well-formed answer to 'your turn'; nothing in the transcript shows he meant the singular, and if he only swallowed the -a of غرفة that is S4 pronunciation. She confirmed بالغلط and moved on.

row.amal_said: ليش؟ You would ruin it? ... one T. ... اه، راح تخربيها.
row.why: In 'if you put too much salt in the soup you will ruin it' he left the object off the transitive verb; she prompted 'You would ruin it?', he added -ha (rah titkharabiha, 56:46), she trimmed the doubled t and confirmed راح تخربيها (56:55). The 'two T' remark is a stutter/prefix doubling, not a second row.
